statement: Old Babylonian mathematical tablets preserve reciprocal tables, multiplication exercises, and sophisticated numerical problem-solving; this is direct evidence of a trained mathematical scribal tradition.

sources.citation: CDLI P257396, Old Babylonian mathematical reciprocal tablet from Nippur.
sources.author: Cuneiform Digital Library Initiative

sources.citation: Columbia University Libraries, Plimpton 322 exhibition description, tablet written around 1800 BCE at Larsa and notable for complex Old Babylonian mathematics.
sources.author: Columbia University Libraries

notes: The claim is about documented specialist mathematics, not the mathematical competence of every inhabitant.
